transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-20
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Jonah Park (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CTO - Timberline), Lea Gomez (Head of MLOps), Tom Reinhardt (Platform Eng), Sofia Marin (Security Lead)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on staging/onboarding steps, security gating (KMS, SOC2-ish questions), VPC peering and runbook timeline. Technical focus on inference latency targets, batching and caching suggestions for their conversational agent workload. Agreement to run a connectivity test and have Redwood propose a small staging footprint.

Topics:
- Staging topology and connectivity
- Security controls: SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs: batch sizes, quantization proposals
- Rollout plan and success metrics

Action items (captured verbally during call): see metadata above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: All right, hey everybody thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, um, appreciate you carving out time. Jonah and I will run through the plan for the onboarding huddle.
[00:14] Raj: Thanks Maya, yeah we, we appreciate you guys. We've been looking forward to getting the staging hooked up, Lea's on because she owns the MLOps pieces.
[00:23] Lea: Hey all. Quick context — we're pushing a beta for a conversational insights assistant for our enterprise customers. Primary constraint is P95 latency under 1.1 seconds for 512 token prompts, and we want to keep cost within our current spend target.
[00:38] Jonah: Got it, thanks Lea. That latency target is helpful. We'll propose a small staging footprint that hits that P95 with a mix of streaming and batching. We'll also recommend cache prefixes to reduce repeated prefix cost.
[00:52] Tom: When you say "caching prefixes" is that the KV cache you're referring to or a full response cache?
[00:58] Jonah: Mostly KV/prefix caching — to keep token generation warm between similar prompts. We can sketch an approach where recent session keys are pinned in memory to avoid cold KV reads. There are tradeoffs though with memory footprint.
[01:13] Sofia: I want to jump in on the sec questions early — SOC2 is on our list, but also we need to make sure the KMS usage and audit logs are available because our compliance team will want proof of key rotation and envelope encryption.
[01:27] Maya: Absolutely. We have a KMS integration pattern for Redwood Private and Dedicated that supports customer-managed KMS, we've also got audit log exports. I'll share the security docs after the call.
[01:40] Raj: Are the audit logs available in a raw S3 export or do you push them into something like a SIEM? Our standard is to forward to Splunk.
[01:48] Maya: We can do both — raw export plus a Splunk forwarder pattern. We'll include that in the runbook.
[01:55] Lea: On networking, we plan to do VPC peering with a tightly restricted route table. Do you prefer peering or transit gateway?
[02:05] Jonah: For the staging footprint peering is simplest and lower friction. For production at scale transit gateway can make sense. We'll document both and recommend peering for initial pilot.
[02:16] Tom: Any pre-reqs from our side for the VPC peering?
[02:19] Maya: Mostly CIDR ranges, a bastion/egress plan, and the IPs for the staging frontends. We'll put a checklist in the pre-config doc.
[02:31] [crosstalk]
[02:34] Raj: Quick question about models — we're evaluating an open Llama-ish model, size 7B quantized. Given Redwood's offering, is that something you validate?
[02:45] Jonah: Yep we onboard open LLMs all the time; note that execution characteristics differ when you quantize to 4-bit. We'll run a short micro-benchmark (latency + token throughput) in our staging env. Also, if you need lower latency we can point to a 13B variant or a tuned 7B variant we've verified.
[03:02] Lea: Would switching to 13B blow up cost? Our cost target is tight.
[03:08] Jonah: It will increase per-token compute but sometimes you can shrink batch sizes and get latency without proportionally raising cost. Also quantization profiles and kernel selection matter — Redwood has optimized kernels for these models but the numbers vary.
[03:24] Maya: To add — our Optimize tooling can recommend pre-configured quantization and batching combos by workload; we'll surface that after the micro-benchmark.
[03:33] Sofia: Can you support customer-managed HSM or only cloud KMS? For our financial customers HSM-backed keys are a must.
[03:42] Maya: We integrate with cloud KMS primarily but we do have an HSM path for Private deployments; it's part of the enterprise packaging. We'll flag that to the solutions team and share the integration notes.
[03:54] Raj: OK good. Next, timeline — we're targeting a pilot with a small customer cohort in late July, so we need staging by early July. Is that feasible?
[04:05] Maya: Yes that seems reasonable. Jonah, how much time do you want for the micro-benchmark and staging verification?
[04:12] Jonah: Realistically two weeks for micro-benchmarks once we have peered network and sample model weights. Then a week for stabilization — so if we start last week of June we should be green by early July.
[04:23] Lea: Sounds tight but doable. We'll try to get you the weights and a sample prompt set by Friday.
[04:29] [00:04:30] Maya: Quick note — please obv strip PII from sample prompts, or mark them and we'll redact on our side.
[04:40] Raj: Yep we'll sanitize.
[04:42] Tom: Are there known restrictions for on-prem vs cloud? We're considering an eventual Private deployment behind our network.
[04:50] Jonah: On-prem requires a different packaging and a private control plane, but from an inference runtime perspective most of the config is identical. Network and KMS are the bigger differences. For Private we can do air-gapped patterns and HSM.
[05:05] Lea: For the rollout plan, can you outline success criteria you'd recommend for the pilot?
[05:11] Maya: Sure — sample success metrics: P95 latency < target (1.1s), mean token cost under your threshold, no critical errors in 7-day smoke tests, and baseline safety regressions per eval harness. We'll include these as suggested KPIs.
[05:26] Raj: On the evals — do you run evals automatically or we run ours?
[05:31] Jonah: We can run an initial suite using your prompt set but we encourage running your domain-specific evals. Redwood also has regression alerting tied to prompt sets so we'll help you set that up.
[05:44] Sofia: Two security items: SSO with SAML is required, plus role-based access control so only ops people can launch workloads. Do you support SCIM for provisioning?
[05:56] Maya: Yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning users. RBAC is configurable at the org and project level. We'll attach SSO and SCIM config docs.
[06:06] [06:06] Raj: Good. How about observability — what's the typical retention for token-level traces?
[06:12] Jonah: By default we keep high-res token traces for 30 days, and aggregated metrics for longer. There's an add-on for extended retention if you need 90/180 day storage.
[06:23] Lea: We'll likely want the token traces for the pilot to debug truncation and prompt-engineering issues.
[06:28] Maya: Noted we'll include a step in the runbook to enable token-level traces for the staging project.
[06:35] Tom: Any prefs for container image or model format? We're mostly using torchscript and int8 artifacts.
[06:42] Jonah: We accept standard model formats and can help with conversion. The runtime will pick best kernels for quantized int8/4bit weights if the model uses supported ops. We'll flag ops that may fall back to slower kernels in our micro-benchmark report.
[06:58] Raj: Earlier you mentioned rollouts and canaries — how does that work in Redwood?
[07:03] Maya: You can define rollout policies per model: percent-based canaries, automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant on error or latency spikes, and A/B routing. The console gives per-route dashboards so you can see latency and cost impact in near real-time.
[07:17] Lea: Will the canary traffic be isolated to avoid hitting our rate limits?
[07:21] Jonah: Yes you can pin canary traffic to a dedicated capacity or limit it by token budget.
[07:27] Sofia: On compliance again — do you provide attestations for key access? We need to demonstrate that no one at Redwood can access unencrypted customer payloads.
[07:36] Maya: For Private deployment yes we support encryption-in-use and customer-managed keys. For hosted there's strong separation and audit controls but if you need a full no-access guarantee we recommend Private. We'll detail the guarantees and the SOC2 report excerpts.
[07:54] Raj: OK excellent. Any blockers you foresee that we should unblock now?
[07:59] Jonah: Biggest blocker is network peering details and model weights. Also sample prompt sets for evals. If you can get those in the next week we're in good shape.
[08:09] Lea: We'll aim to share weights and sanitized prompts by Friday. Sofia will share KMS contact.
[08:16] Sofia: Yep I'll loop in our KMS admin.
[08:19] Maya: Great. On deliverables I'll send a pre-config checklist, runbook, and a proposed staging topology. Jonah will add the micro-benchmark plan.
[08:29] Raj: Can we get an estimate of cost for the pilot? Even a ballpark for the staging footprint would be helpful.
[08:36] Jonah: We'll put together a pilot price estimate — it depends on model size and throughput. I'll give a conservative number in the runbook but expect accuracy after the micro-benchmark.
[08:49] [08:49] Maya: Quick note — competitors you mentioned earlier, some customers compare with BigCloud AI and FastServe; we often highlight our cost controls and rollout safety as differentiators.
[08:59] Raj: Understood.
[09:01] Lea: Any final questions?
[09:04] Tom: Just one about SLA — for Dedicated what's the uptime SLA?
[09:10] Maya: Dedicated comes with an SLA in the enterprise contract — 99.9 for availability and latency SLOs we can agree on per model tier. We'll surface the SLA language.
[09:20] Sofia: And incident response — do you have 24/7 support for pilot customers?
[09:25] Maya: For pilots we provide business-hours support and on-call for critical incidents; enterprise add-on gives 24/7. We'll detail support tiers in the follow-up.
[09:36] Raj: Great. I think that's it. Thanks everyone.

Recap / Next steps (verbal):
- Redwood: share onboarding runbook, SSO/SCIM & KMS docs, staging topology, and a pilot cost estimate by 2027-06-22.
- Customer: provide model weights, sanitized prompt set, VPC peering details (CIDR and contacts), and KMS admin contact by 2027-06-24.
- Schedule connectivity test for week of 2027-06-28 (30 min).

Close:
[09:45] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the connectivity test and send the doc pack.
[09:51] Raj: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash") and product names transcribed inconsistently ("Redwood Private" sometimes appears as "Redwood private"), filler words retained.
